summary: A first-week one-on-one with the manager is followed by a bigger work network and more teamwork.
realLife: A Microsoft analysis of about 3,000 new hires, as summarized by Atlassian, linked a first-week manager one-on-one to a larger internal network, better meetings and more collaboration.
sources: Atlassian Work Life, starting a new job and first week success: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/teamwork/starting-a-new-job-and-first-week-success
inGame: Needs: a tie-growth read tied to tenure; the coworker ties between people at one workplace can carry it, aged by tenure in the job record (employer, position, workplace, pay, tenure) in the jobs module. Scene: needs a producer for first-day-ropes.

turns.summary: The manager is too busy and the first-week one-on-one slips away.
turns.writesBack: The newcomer's network stays small, and the manager tie stays thin.

turns.summary: The one-on-one covers tasks only, with no talk about people or the team.
turns.writesBack: The newcomer learns the job but meets few coworkers, and ties grow slowly.

turns.summary: The manager uses the meeting to walk the newcomer around and name each coworker.
turns.writesBack: Several coworker ties form at once, and the newcomer feels welcome.
